meal.name: Sunday Roast Chicken
meal.workflow_md:
*Anchored to 8:00 PM service · chicken is the clock · pasta & salad built into the rest window · dessert assembled ahead, torched at service* ## T-Minus Timeline
TimeAction
T-24 hrDry-brine both birds: ~9–10 g salt each, uncovered on racks in fridge with airflow (target 18–24 hr; 30 hr hard stop)
T-3 to 4 hrAssemble dessert pots: jam base, sweetened yogurt over, level surface, chill (holds up to 4 hr; do NOT torch yet)
T-120Pull both birds from fridge — temper on counter (full 60 min)
T-75Preheat oven 450°F / 232°C
T-65Pat both birds bone-dry, truss, pepper skin (no re-salt). Insert ThermoWorks leave-in probe into the breast of one bird — thickest part, off the bone; set high alarm ~150°F / 66°C
T-60Both birds into oven on wire racks set over trays, side by side with a gap — roast to breast temp, ~40–55 min
T-30Prep salad: wash and dry leaves, hold in fridge; whisk vinaigrette, set aside
T-20Leave-in probe alarms near ~150°F. Spot-check the second bird's breast with the Thermapen (one probe watches one bird)
T-8Birds out at breast temp — add thyme to pan, single baste. Rest uncovered (15 min; dinner bird carves at T-0, lunch bird cools for fridge)
T-8Induction #1: pasta water on to boil (salted lightly). Induction #2: oil + garlic, low (2 min)
T-6Add anchovies to garlic oil — cook to just-coloring garlic (~3 min), then off-heat (skillet stays as finishing pan)
T-6Spaghetti into water — cook firm-tender (~9–10 min); reserve ¼ cup water before draining
T-3Warm plates. Carve dinner bird; spoon a little warm pan juice over the breast (not the skin)
T-1Transfer drained pasta into anchovy skillet — lemon juice + zest, splash of pasta water, emulsify off-heat, pepper
T-0Dress salad, plate the three savoury dishes. Parsley over pasta; vinaigrette & pan juices beside the chicken
DessertAfter mains clear: sugar the chilled pots and torch to amber, one at a time; rest 1 min to set, serve (torch only at service)
## Failure Prioritisation *If the plating window slips, pasta fails first — it clumps and its oil breaks as it cools; the dressed salad wilts second. The chicken tolerates the wait best, so plate it first. The dessert is decoupled — assembled hours ahead, torched only when the mains are done.* ## Workflow Notes **Critical path:** The chicken governs — dry-brine → temper → roast both birds to breast temp (150–152°F / 66–67°C) → mandatory 15-min uncovered rest. Pasta and salad build inside that rest window; never hold the chicken for a side. Dessert is fully decoupled: assembled hours ahead, torched once the mains clear. **Oven & heat sequencing:** Single oven state throughout — 450°F / 232°C, the two birds on wire racks over trays, side by side with a gap for airflow, no transitions. No pasta water until the birds are out resting, so oven and induction never contend. Induction #1 owns the pasta pot; Induction #2 owns the anchovy skillet, which doubles as the finishing pan (off-heat before pasta lands). The butane torch finishes the dessert at service. If the garlic races, pull it off-heat first — scorched garlic oil is unrecoverable. **Thermometers:** ThermoWorks leave-in probe in one bird's breast (alarm ~150°F / 66°C) as the primary gate; Thermapen instant-read to spot-check the second bird. One leave-in probe watches one bird only. ## Holding Chain
ComponentHold StrategyMax HoldDrift RiskCorrective
Chicken (post-rest)Uncovered on board, carved late15 min ideal, 25 maxSkin softens if tented; meat coolsDo not tent. Carve just before serving. Past 20 min, warm plates
Anchovy oil baseSkillet off-heat, residual warm10 minGarlic bitters if re-heatedHold off-heat; pasta finishes in it — no re-fry
Pasta (in skillet)Do not hold0 minClumps, oil dullsTime drain to skillet being ready; emulsify and plate immediately
Salad leaves (undressed)Fridge, dry, in bowl60 minWilt if dressed earlyKeep leaves and vinaigrette separate until T-0
VinaigretteRoom temp, whisk before use2 hrSeparates on standingRe-whisk before dressing
Dessert pots (un-torched)Fridge, chilled, levelled4 hrYogurt weeps if held too longPour off surface whey before sugaring
Torched crustTorch to order~10 minCrust weeps on cold yogurtTorch only at service, one at a time; serve within minutes
meal.shared_prep_md:
**Lemon:** 1–2 lemons total — zest ½ + 1½ tsp juice → pasta; 1½ tbsp juice → vinaigrette; reserve a wedge for the table

**Parsley:** 1 bunch — chop ~6 tbsp → pasta finish (doubled for freshness against the roast)

**Garlic:** 4 large cloves, minced → pasta only

**Thyme:** 2 tsp minced per bird → chicken pan (optional, Keller)

**Dijon:** 1 tbsp → vinaigrette

*Shopping-list notes: Two Huber's birds (~1.07 kg each) — salt ~9–10 g per bird, ~18–20 g total; one carved for dinner, one for next-day lunch. One tin of anchovies covers the pasta with fillets to spare. One–two lemons cover pasta and vinaigrette. Salad uses extra-virgin for the vinaigrette; pasta can use regular olive oil. Dessert: Odette jam on hand; caster sugar and yogurt the only additions. No rice component in this meal.*

dishes.name: Roast Chicken
dishes.source: Recovered from roast-chicken-sunday.docx (no generation date stated in doc; menu cooked Sunday 2026-07-06)
dishes.summary: Thomas Keller's austere 450°F roast chicken with an 18–24 hr uncovered dry-brine, no basting, and a breast-temperature pull at 150–152°F; two ~1.07 kg Huber's birds roasted side by side, one for dinner and one for next-day lunch.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Keller's austere high-heat roast — crackling salted skin over juicy meat, no basting — with an overnight dry-brine and a breast-temperature pull for even seasoning and a reliably juicy breast. Two small birds roasted side by side; one carved for dinner, one for next-day lunch. Menu line: **Roast Chicken** — Keller method, overnight dry-brine, breast-temp pull; two Huber's birds, one for dinner, one for next-day lunch. ## Yield & Timing *Serves 3 + next-day lunch · Two birds ~1.07 kg each (Huber's, 2.14 kg combined) · Total ~24 hr (mostly passive) · Active ~20 min · Temper 60 min · Roast ~40–55 min · Rest 15 min · Oven 450°F / 232°C* ## Prep Phase **1. Dry-brine (both birds), T-24 hr.** Pat each bird very dry, inside and out. Weigh ~9–10 g salt per bird; rain ~85% over the skin from height, the rest in the cavity. Set both breast-up on racks over trays, **uncovered**, in the fridge — target 18–24 hr, 30 hr hard stop. *Give each bird airflow — do not crowd or stack. Past 30 hr on a bird this small turns the texture ham-like.* **2. Temper, T-120.** Counter, full 60 min, to take the chill off both. *A fridge-cold bird roasts unevenly and steams; small birds still want the full hour for an even centre.* **3. Final prep, T-65.** Re-pat each skin bone-dry. Truss. Pepper the skin. **Do not re-salt** — the dry-brine has seasoned through. Insert the ThermoWorks leave-in probe into the breast of one bird — thickest part, tip centred, off the bone — and set the high alarm to ~150°F / 66°C. ## Active Cooking **1. Roast (both birds), T-60.** Oven fully at 450°F / 232°C. Set each bird on a **wire rack over a shallow tray**, side by side with a few cm gap. *The rack lets air circulate underneath so the skin crisps rather than steams; the tray catches the jus for basting and the carved breast. Do not sit the bird flat in a solid pan — the underside steams. Do not stack on a second rack.* **No basting, no added butter** — added fat steams and softens the skin. **2. Monitor by probe.** The leave-in probe in the first bird alarms at ~150°F / 66°C — no need to check it repeatedly. When it nears the alarm, **spot-check the second bird's breast with the Thermapen**, since one leave-in probe watches only one bird and they may not finish together. *Skin should be fully browned by ~40 min for a ~1 kg bird; colour corroborates the probe.* **3. Out and rest, T-8.** At breast temp, add thyme to the pan and give one baste with pan juices. Rest **uncovered** on a board, breast-up, 15 min. *Carve the dinner bird first; the lunch bird cools fully before refrigerating.* *Doneness (primary gate = breast): Pull when the breast reads 150–152°F / 66–67°C; carries to ~155°F / 68°C during the rest. Thighs read ~165–175°F / 74–79°C by then, correct for dark meat. Secondary cue: thigh-joint juices run clear; legs loose in the socket. If the breast is at temp but thigh juices run pink, tent only the legs and give 5 more min.* ## Holding & Assembly Rest 15 min uncovered on a board (catches carving juices; tenting steams the skin). Remove twine. Carve per Keller: separate wing joints, remove legs and thighs, lift the oysters, split the breast down the middle and serve each half on the bone with a wing joint attached. **Slather the carved meat — not the skin — with fresh butter.** Spoon a little warm pan juice over the breast meat, avoiding the skin; reserve the rest for the table. Serve the lemon-Dijon vinaigrette *beside* the chicken, not over the skin. *Carve within ~3 min of serving so the skin doesn't soften.* ## Critical Control Points
ClassFailure ModeSensory CueRecovery
CriticalSkin steams instead of crisps — pale, flabby, no crackle.Skin slack and blond after ~40 min in the oven.Largely unrecoverable once roasted wet. Prevent: 18–24 hr uncovered dry-brine + re-pat dry + no in-roast basting + no tenting at rest + butter/juice on meat, not skin.
MajorBreast dries chasing thigh doneness. Unrecoverable for breast if pushed past; dish remains serviceable.Breast climbs past 155°F / 68°C before the pull.Pull on breast at 150–152°F, not the thigh; tent only the legs if they lag.
MajorBirds crowd the oven — touching or too close, they steam rather than crisp.Pale, soft skin between the birds even as tops brown.Roast side by side with a gap; if the Bosch can't fit both with clearance, roast the lunch bird after the dinner bird.
MajorSalt over-concentrates on a small bird.Skin tastes sharply salty pre-roast.Hold to ~9–10 g per bird; don't re-salt at T-65; unsalted butter at carving buffers.
MinorUneven browning — one side pale.Visible at the browning check.Rotate the pan; give 3–5 min more; acceptable cosmetic variance.
## Adjustment Notes
AdjustmentGuidance
SaltIf skin reads under-seasoned, a light finishing-salt pinch at carving recovers it — the dry-brine should prevent this.
AcidIf the jus tastes flat, a few drops of reserved lemon lift it.
RichnessSelf-buffers at the table via butter, pan juices, and vinaigrette served separately.
Lunch birdCool fully uncovered before refrigerating; eats well cold next day (use-by 07/07, keep to Monday).
## Scaling Notes Toward the top of the size range, add 5–10 min and verify by breast temp, not clock. Salt scales with weight — hold 0.8–1.0%. Do not dry-brine past ~30 hr on a small bird. Two birds need oven clearance between them; if unavailable, roast sequentially.

dishes.name: Anchovy Spaghetti
dishes.source: Recovered from roast-chicken-sunday.docx (no generation date stated in doc; menu cooked Sunday 2026-07-06)
dishes.summary: Spaghetti tossed off-heat in a low-cooked garlic and anchovy oil with lemon juice, zest, a splash of pasta water and doubled parsley; Parmesan deliberately omitted against the salted roast chicken.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview A garlic-and-anchovy oil sauce clinging to firm spaghetti, lifted with lemon juice, zest, and doubled parsley — the umami, acid, and freshness the austere chicken lacks. Salt kept low against the salted bird. Menu line: **Anchovy Spaghetti** — garlic, olive oil, lemon, doubled parsley; finished in the skillet. ## Yield & Timing *Serves 3 (2 restrained + 1 full) · Total ~15 min · Active ~15 min · Induction (both burners)* ## Prep Phase Mince garlic. Chop 6–8 anchovies. Chop parsley (~6 tbsp). Zest ½ lemon; juice 1½ tsp. *All done during the chicken's roast so the rest window is pure execution.* ## Active Cooking *Both induction burners run concurrently — pot boils on #1, oil base builds on #2. The base skillet becomes the finishing pan: off-heat before the pasta lands so the garlic doesn't re-fry.* **1. Base (Induction #2, low).** Heat oil, add garlic, cook gently 2 min — *pale gold, never brown.* Add anchovies; cook until garlic just begins to color, ~3 min, stirring so the fillets melt in. Pull **off-heat** — leave it in the skillet. **2. Pasta (Induction #1).** Boil lightly salted water. Cook spaghetti firm-tender (just past the bite), ~9–10 min. Reserve **¼ cup / 60 ml** pasta water before draining. **3. Finish in the skillet.** With the skillet off-heat (or barely warm), transfer the drained pasta straight in. Add lemon juice + zest and a splash of pasta water. Toss vigorously to emulsify and coat. Pepper. *Should sheen and cling, not pool — add pasta water a splash at a time only if dry. The skillet must not be hot or the garlic turns bitter.* **4.** Plate; parsley over the top. ## Holding & Assembly Do not hold. Finished last, plated last — toss and serve within ~1 min of draining. *Even 3–4 min of holding clumps the pasta and dulls the oil.* Omit Parmesan with this menu — chicken + anchovy + Parmesan stacks salt and umami with no upside; the pasta is a support act. ## Critical Control Points
ClassFailure ModeSensory CueRecovery
CriticalGarlic scorches — bitter, acrid oil. The oil is the sauce.Garlic browns past gold, oil smells sharp; or pasta added to a hot skillet.Keep base heat low; anchovies in at 2 min; skillet off-heat before the pasta lands. Unrecoverable once scorched.
MajorSauce breaks / oily — no cling, oil pools on the plate.Pasta greasy, sauce won't coat.Add reserved pasta water a splash at a time, toss hard off-heat to re-emulsify the starch-oil bond.
MajorOver-salted from anchovy + salted water against the salted bird.Aggressively salty on the plate.Prevent: salt the water lightly, no sauce salt, no Parmesan. If salty, add lemon + parsley to cut.
MinorPasta overcooked / soft.No bite.Pull at firm-tender; it softens slightly in the hot toss.
## Adjustment Notes
AdjustmentGuidance
SaltWithheld from the sauce — taste at the toss, correct only at the table given the salted bird. If flat rather than salty, a few drops of lemon before any salt.
AcidLemon at the toss; add a touch more to brighten if the dish reads heavy.
RichnessToo lean or sharp → another tablespoon of the warm oil base; too rich → more lemon and parsley.
## Scaling Notes Anchovy salt scales non-linearly — don't scale fillet count linearly on a bigger batch; taste at 1.5×. A wider skillet keeps garlic in a single layer and prevents scorch; crowded oil heats unevenly.

dishes.name: Bitter Leaf Salad, Lemon-Dijon Vinaigrette
dishes.source: Recovered from roast-chicken-sunday.docx (no generation date stated in doc; menu cooked Sunday 2026-07-06)
dishes.summary: Little gem, frisée and a minority of Belgian endive dressed at T-0 with a 1½:4:1 lemon:oil:Dijon vinaigrette — the fresh, acid, crunch axis against the roast chicken and oil-based pasta.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Cold, crisp mixed bitter leaves in a sharp lemon-Dijon vinaigrette — the meal's relief valve, cutting the chicken fat and oil-based pasta with bitterness and acid. Meal-level carve-out: this is the fresh/acid/crunch axis the two cooked components lack. Menu line: **Bitter Leaf Salad** — little gem, frisée, endive; lemon-Dijon vinaigrette. ## Yield & Timing *Serves 3 · Total ~10 min · Active ~10 min · No heat* ## Prep Phase Wash and thoroughly **dry** the leaves (a wet leaf won't hold dressing) at T-30; hold in the fridge. Tear frisée and larger leaves to bite size; keep little gem in short ribbons; separate endive leaves or halve lengthwise. Whisk the vinaigrette: Dijon + lemon first, then stream in the oil to emulsify; season with the pinch of salt and pepper. Hold at room temp. *Little gem for sweet crunch and body, frisée for delicate bitterness, endive as the crisp bitter accent — keep it a minority.* ## Active Cooking Not applicable — no heat. Assembly only. ## Holding & Assembly Keep leaves and vinaigrette **separate** until the last moment. At T-0, dress lightly — leaves just coated, not wet — toss, and plate immediately. *Reserve a little vinaigrette to spoon beside the chicken. Dress only what will be eaten; undressed spares keep, dressed leaves wilt within minutes.* ## Critical Control Points
ClassFailure ModeSensory CueRecovery
MajorLeaves dressed too early — wilted, soggy. Unrecoverable for wilted leaves; hold back undressed spares.Leaves limp and weeping before serving.Dress at T-0 only.
MinorVinaigrette split — oil separates.Dressing looks broken, won't cling.Re-whisk before dressing; the Dijon re-emulsifies it.
MinorOver-dressed — heavy, oily leaves.Dressing pools at the bowl base.Dress lightly, in stages; serve extra on the side.
## Adjustment Notes
AdjustmentGuidance
AcidIf the plate reads rich, sharpen with a few drops of lemon; if too sharp against the wine, round with a little more oil.
SaltStays minimal; the Dijon and the meal's other salted components carry it.
## Scaling Notes Vinaigrette holds the ~1½:4:1 lemon:oil:Dijon ratio at any volume. Dress-to-order regardless of batch size — never pre-dress expecting leftovers to hold.

dishes.name: Torched-Sugar Yogurt Pots, Odette Jam
dishes.source: Recovered from roast-chicken-sunday.docx (no generation date stated in doc; menu cooked Sunday 2026-07-06)
dishes.summary: Three ramekins of lightly sweetened full-fat Greek yogurt over 2 tsp Odette dark-fruit jam, chilled up to 4 hr, then topped with 1 tsp caster sugar and torched to amber one at a time at service.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Chilled tangy yogurt over a base of Odette dark-fruit jam, finished with a thin torched-sugar crust cracked at the table — a cool, tart-sweet reset after the rich savoury meal. Menu line: **Torched-Sugar Yogurt Pots, Odette Jam** — chilled yogurt over dark-fruit jam, brûléed sugar lid cracked at the table. ## Yield & Timing *Serves 3 · Total ~15 min + 20 min chill · Active ~10 min · Butane torch finish, no cook* ## Prep Phase **1.** Stir the yogurt with honey/icing sugar to a light sweetness — *taste; it should stay tangy, not dessert-sweet. The jam carries the sweetness.* **2.** Spoon 2 tsp jam into the base of each of three torch-safe ramekins; spread to cover. **3.** Spoon ~115 g sweetened yogurt over the jam in each; level the surface flat. *A flat surface torches evenly.* Chill 20 min uncovered to firm the surface (holds up to 4 hr). ## Active Cooking *No cook — butane torch finish only, to order. Do this after the mains have cleared, one pot at a time.* **1.** Sprinkle 1 tsp caster sugar in a thin, even layer across each chilled pot. *Use caster, not icing sugar — icing sugar scorches.* **2.** Torch, moving continuously, until the sugar melts and turns amber. *Stop at deep gold — black flecks are bitter. Done when it stops bubbling and sets glassy-matte within a few seconds of pulling the flame away.* **3.** Rest 1 min to harden into a crisp sheet. Finish with a little lemon zest if using. ## Holding & Assembly Assemble and chill up to 4 hr ahead — the surface holds. **Torch only at service:** the crust weeps and dissolves within ~15 min of contact with the cold yogurt. Serve immediately, cracking the crust at the table. *Torch one pot at a time; a torched pot cannot wait.* ## Critical Control Points
ClassFailure ModeSensory CueRecovery
MajorSugar crust won't crisp — layer too thick, still syrupy. Unrecoverable if pooled; scrape and redo.Stays wet, no glassy set after torching.Sprinkle thin and even; torch longer with continuous motion.
MajorTorched too far — acrid, burnt.Black flecks, bitter smell.Stop at deep amber; keep the flame moving. Unrecoverable once burnt — wipe and re-sugar.
MinorYogurt weeps / watery surface.Liquid pooling before torching.Use thick full-fat Greek yogurt; pour off any whey before sugaring.
## Adjustment Notes
AdjustmentGuidance
SweetnessIf too sweet against the meal, the yogurt was over-sweetened — a few drops of lemon or zest pulls it back.
Acid / balanceIf too tart, a thread more jam at the base rather than more sugar.
TextureKeep the crust thin; it is contrast, not a sugar hit.
## Scaling Notes Scales linearly by pot. Torch one pot at a time regardless of batch — the crust must be crisp at service. For more than ~4 pots, torch in the kitchen in quick succession rather than at the table.
